issues: Severe nocturnal hypoglycemia between 23:00 and 03:00 (Time Below Range reaching 11.4% to 18.5%).
Severe evening hypoglycemia between 18:00 and 19:00 (Time Below Range reaching 7.7% to 15.3%).
Aggressive target drop to 90 mg/dL starting at 23:00, leaving zero safety buffer for nighttime glucose fluctuations.
Extremely permissive safety limits (max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U) combined with Dynamic ISF, allowing dangerous UAM insulin stacking against GLP-1 delayed meals.
summary: The data shows severe evening and nocturnal hypoglycemia, primarily driven by a very tight 90 mg/dL overnight target and highly permissive safety limits. Because zero carbohydrates are logged, the system uses the Unannounced Meal (UAM) algorithm exclusively. The delayed gastric emptying caused by GLP-1 leads the UAM algorithm to over-deliver insulin during prolonged glucose rises, resulting in crashes once the insulin outpaces the delayed absorption.
education: GLP-1 medications significantly delay carbohydrate absorption, flattening and extending the glucose rise after a meal.

When relying entirely on the Unannounced Meal (UAM) algorithm without carb logging, the system responds to rising glucose by microbolusing. If absorption is delayed, the insulin can peak after the glucose stops rising, causing a steep crash.
A target of 90 mg/dL overnight leaves virtually no margin for error. Even minor over-corrections from the algorithm can push glucose below 70 mg/dL.
strengths: Excellent sensor coverage at 98.7% with very few gaps.
Stable morning fasting control with Time in Range between 95% and 98% from 04:00 to 08:00.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Raising targets and clamping safety limits will likely increase daytime average glucose in the short term, but this is a necessary step to eliminate severe hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.evidence: 14-day period with 98.7% coverage, 3995 entries, and comprehensive loop telemetry.
analysis_steps.findings: Data quality is excellent for sensor and loop execution. However, there are zero logged carbohydrate entries, indicating a fully unannounced meal strategy.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of meal carbohydrate logging.

analysis_steps.evidence: TBR exceeds 5.1% overall, clustering severely at 00:00-03:00 (10-18% TBR) and 18:00-19:00 (7-15% TBR). Minimum glucose reaches 41-42 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.findings: The safety profile is heavily compromised by recurring deep hypoglycemia in the early evening and early night, necessitating immediate target and limit adjustments.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: None strictly for basic safety metrics.

analysis_steps.evidence: Target segments drop to 90 mg/dL at 23:00 and stay there until 08:00.
analysis_steps.findings: The aggressive 90 mg/dL target starting at 23:00 aligns exactly with the onset of the most severe nighttime hypoglycemia cluster. It provides no safety buffer against UAM or Dynamic ISF corrections.

analysis_steps.evidence: Flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U all day. DIA is 10h. CR is 10.5-13.2 g/U but inactive proactively due to zero carbs.
analysis_steps.findings: With zero announced carbs, CR is largely dormant. The flat 56 ISF is heavily modified by the Dynamic ISF feature, driving aggressive corrections that the profile baseline alone does not explain.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of meal sizes prevents true Carb Ratio evaluation.

analysis_steps.evidence: smb_always_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true. Loop logs show constant UAM Boost triggers.
analysis_steps.findings: AAPS is handling all meals via UAM. The algorithm repeatedly stacks microboluses to fight glucose rises that are unnaturally prolonged by the GLP-1 medication.
Safety constraints are set dangerously wide. A 12 U/h limit against a 0.6 U/h basal allows massive insulin dumping, which directly causes the evening and nighttime crashes when UAM overcompensates.

analysis_steps.evidence: Zero carb entries and no declared meal strategies in the context.
analysis_steps.findings: There is no active meal bolus strategy to review. The system is relying entirely on UAM reacting to post-meal glucose slopes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Total absence of meal logging and strategy declarations.

analysis_steps.findings: Cannot analyze e-carb configurations or precise absorption curves without logged meal timestamps and sizes.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Missing all meal composition and timing data.

analysis_steps.evidence: Combination of GLP-1 delayed absorption, fully unannounced meals, extreme safety limits, and tight 90 mg/dL targets.
analysis_steps.findings: The most immediate safety step is to raise the overnight targets to establish a buffer against lows. In a subsequent iteration, the extreme safety limits must be clamped. Meal logging must begin to map true absorption patterns.

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Glucose Targets
recommendations.description: The current 90 mg/dL target starting at 23:00 leaves zero room for error and correlates precisely with the highest rates of nocturnal hypoglycemia. Raising this to 100 mg/dL restores a flat, safer baseline.

recommendations.title: Restrict Max Basal and Max IOB (Requires separate review)
recommendations.description: The limits of 12 U/h for basal and 25 U for IOB are disproportionately large compared to the base profile. This allows the UAM algorithm to dump dangerous amounts of insulin for delayed meals. These should be reviewed and lowered significantly in the next optimization step.

profile_recommendation.rationale: The 90 mg/dL target starting at 23:00 directly triggers aggressive overnight corrections that lead to severe hypoglycemia (11.4% to 18.5% TBR). Raising it to 100 mg/dL aligns with the daytime target and establishes a critical safety buffer.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe overnight Time Below Range for 3-5 days to confirm severe lows are mitigated before making any basal or safety limit adjustments.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Change the profile targets at 23:00 and 00:00 from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: While highly dangerous, altering these limits concurrently with the target changes violates sequential safety adjustments. Ensure targets are tested first, then aggressively clamp these values in the next review.
Dynamic ISF is reacting correctly to unannounced highs, though the magnitude is dangerous because of the loose safety limits. Maintain current settings while targets are adjusted.

implementation_steps: Change the 23:00 and 00:00 glucose targets from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL to establish a safer, flat overnight baseline.
Observe overnight glucose patterns for 3 to 5 days to confirm that nocturnal severe hypoglycemia is resolved.
In the next iteration, strongly consider working with the care team to clamp max_basal_u_per_hour and max_iob_units to safely restrict UAM over-delivery.
Begin logging meal times (even as 0-carb entries) to create a visual record of how severely GLP-1 delays absorption before the UAM peaks.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Since zero carbs are logged, the system functions entirely on Unannounced Meals (UAM). GLP-1 delays the glucose peak, which forces the UAM algorithm to stack insulin early on, culminating in severe crashes hours later when absorption drags on.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Continue relying on UAM for now, but focus heavily on restricting system safety limits to prevent insulin over-stacking against GLP-1 delayed meals.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log actual meal times (even without carb amounts) to map the exact duration of the delay between eating and the UAM-driven glucose peak.
